text:
[name]
Ann Arbor, MI | [email] | [phone] | [url] | [url]

EDUCATION
University of Michigan — Ann Arbor, MI
Ph.D. in Computer Science and Engineering (computer vision and robotics), expected 2028; third year
Adviser: faculty member in the robotics institute; research on self-supervised 3D perception for mobile manipulation
Coursework: Computer Vision, Probabilistic Robotics, Advanced Machine Learning, Convex Optimization; GPA 3.9

Purdue University — West Lafayette, IN
B.S. in Computer Engineering, May 2023 | GPA 3.78, with distinction
Undergraduate research in the computer vision lab (two years); honors thesis on depth completion for LiDAR

RESEARCH EXPERIENCE
Graduate Research Assistant, University of Michigan Robotics | August 2023 – Present
- Developed a self-supervised method for 3D object pose estimation from RGB-D sequences that improved pose accuracy by 11 points over the prior best on a standard benchmark; first-author paper at ICRA 2025
- Built a learned grasp-affordance model that transfers from simulation to a physical arm; 84% grasp success on 40 unseen household objects versus 67% for the baseline; first-author paper at AAAI 2026
- Contributed the data-collection pipeline and the evaluation protocol to a lab paper on language-conditioned manipulation; fourth of seven authors, ICCV 2025
- Released an RGB-D manipulation dataset of 210,000 frames with 6-DoF annotations; about 3,100 downloads and 9 citing papers in the first year
- Co-mentor two undergraduate researchers; one is first author on a submitted workshop paper
- Maintain the lab's shared training cluster (12 GPUs) and the experiment-tracking setup used by 9 students
- Ran the real-robot evaluation campaign for the lab's manipulation work: about 1,400 physical grasp trials on two arms over 6 weeks, with a logging pipeline that reproduces every trial from recorded sensor data
- Passed the qualifying examination in May 2025 with the thesis proposal on self-supervised 3D perception for manipulation

Research Intern, Toyota Research Institute, Robotics Division | May 2025 – August 2025
- Worked on a perception module for a home-assistance robot; reduced depth-estimation error on reflective surfaces by 23% using a learned refinement step
- Internship project led to the AAAI 2026 submission (joint with the Michigan lab); offered a return internship for 2026

Undergraduate Research Assistant, Purdue Computer Vision Lab | August 2021 – May 2023
- Honors thesis on sparse-to-dense depth completion; presented at the Purdue undergraduate research conference (poster)
- Built the lab's LiDAR-camera calibration tool used for two subsequent data-collection efforts

TEACHING
- Graduate Student Instructor, EECS 442 Computer Vision, University of Michigan, Winter 2025 (about 180 students; ran two discussion sections and wrote two programming assignments)
- Teaching assistant, ECE 264 Advanced C Programming, Purdue, Fall 2022

PUBLICATIONS
1. ICRA 2025 — first author (of 4) — self-supervised 6-DoF object pose estimation from RGB-D video
2. AAAI 2026 — first author (of 5) — sim-to-real grasp affordances for unseen objects
3. ICCV 2025 — fourth author (of 7) — language-conditioned mobile manipulation benchmark
4. CVPR 2024 Workshop on Embodied AI — second author (of 3) — dataset paper for RGB-D manipulation
5. arXiv 2026 — first author — preprint under review on cross-embodiment affordance transfer

HONORS
- Rackham Graduate Fellowship, University of Michigan, 2023 – 2024 (first-year funding)
- Best Student Paper finalist, ICRA 2025 (one of 5 finalists)
- Purdue College of Engineering Outstanding Senior in Computer Engineering, 2023

SERVICE
- Reviewer: ICRA 2026, IROS 2025, CVPR 2026 workshops
- Organizer, Michigan Robotics graduate student seminar, 2024 – 2025

SKILLS
Python, PyTorch, C++, ROS 2, CUDA (basic), Isaac Sim, MuJoCo, Open3D, Docker, Linux cluster administration; 3D perception, self-supervised learning, manipulation, sim-to-real transfer
